back: The extra force on one syllable of a word: TEA-cher, ho-TEL, com-PU-ter.
Noun: first syllable (a REcord, an OBject, a PREsent). Verb: second syllable (to reCORD, to obJECT, to preSENT).
Stress the syllable just before the ending: edu-CA-tion, de-CI-sion, eco-NO-mic.
knife, know, knee; write, wrong, wrist; climb, lamb, doubt, debt.

front: Silent h, t, l, n, s, p, d
back: hour, honest; listen, castle; half, calm; autumn, column; island; receipt, psychology; Wednesday.
t after p, k, f, s, sh, ch (walked); d after voiced sounds (played); id after t or d (wanted).
Stress content words (nouns, main verbs, adjectives, adverbs); move the stress to contrast a word: I didn't take YOUR pen.
Falling: statements, commands, wh- questions. Rising: yes/no questions. Lists rise on each item and fall on the last.
Falling tag = expecting agreement (It's hot, isn't it? ↘). Rising tag = a real question (You're coming, aren't you? ↗).
